lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There you are! I aired the entrance hall the moment I heard the gate. Mrs. Bramble — housekeeper, keeper of keys, and the only soul here who still needs a teapot.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The manor rearranges itself overnight, you know. Rooms wander. Doors sulk. You'll want a good breakfast and a better sense of humor.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Your room is the one that stays put — I insisted, and the house respects a woman with a mop. Everything else is negotiable by morning.

nodes.summary: Met Mrs. Bramble, the housekeeper. The rooms wander; the tea does not.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Oh, I like you already. Most guests lead with the wandering rooms.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Manners before mysteries — that's a house rule now. I've just invented it, and I shall enforce it with scones.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Now. Coat off, worries down, and let the house get a look at you. It's been between guests a long while, and so, if I'm honest, have I.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mm. The late master studied words, and words never sit still either. You'll get used to it, dear. Or you won't, and that's its own kind of fun.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Last Tuesday the morning room spent the whole day being an upstairs. No note, no apology. We carry on.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You'll learn the trick of it: hold your plans loosely and your teacup tight. Everything else is furniture.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Tea. Sit. That's the whole of the house rules — the manor invents the rest daily. Milk or lemon? Don't answer; I already know. Housekeepers always know.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There. Told you I knew. Thirty years of pouring for this house — I could serve the drafts their preference, if drafts took cups.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Come by every morning, mind. A day in this place goes better on a full pot, and I hear everything worth hearing before the toast is done.

nodes.summary: Tea with Mrs. Bramble is now a morning ritual.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You came in last night with dusk on your shoulders and not a step left in you. I've seen the master do the very same. The manor keeps what you found — nothing is wasted here, pet.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I left the lamp lit on the stairs for you. Old habit. It's nice, having a reason for the habit again.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Eggs this morning, no arguments. Walking a house empty takes more out of a body than the body admits.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: All the way to empty again? Tsk. Drink this first today. A house this size respects a walker who paces herself. Mostly.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mostly, I say, because the east wing is a flirt and will always coax one more corridor out of you. Don't let it. Or do — but eat first.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There's a flask by the door for today. Tea holds its warmth longer than resolve does, and I've known both to save an afternoon.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Wise, stopping while the light was still gold. The rooms gossip about guests who know when to fold their napkin.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Good gossip, mind. The Gallery called you 'sensible' — from the Gallery that's practically a proposal.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Rest banked is rest spent well here. The house saves your unspent evenings somewhere; I've never found the drawer, but I trust it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: A whole day and the house gave you nothing but locked doors and long looks? It does that. It tested him too, before it trusted him. Eat something.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And don't you go carrying yesterday up the stairs with you. This house forgets its own floor plan nightly — the least you can do is forget one bad afternoon.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Second scone. Medicinal. I'll hear no argument from someone the Gallery outstared.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I heard you speak at the Sanctum door yesterday. The whole house held its breath — the kettle went quiet, and kettles never do. It wasn't the word. But it listened. That's new.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Thirty years I've dusted past that door, and it never once held its breath for me. Whatever you're doing, pet — it's the right kind of wrong.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Tea's stronger this morning. Doors that listen deserve guessers with their wits about them.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You found one of his scraps yesterday, didn't you. Careful with those — not dangerous, mind. Just heavy, the way old handwriting gets.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I used to find them tucked in the oddest places. Under the butter dish, once. I put it back. Some things want finding by the right person.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Seems the house agrees you're the right person. Don't let that go to your head — let it go to your journal.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Not one wrong step in that room yesterday — the floorboards told me before you were down for breakfast. Show-off. Have a scone.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The master had days like that. He'd come down trying not to smile and fail at it magnificently. You're doing the very same face, dear.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I shan't make a fuss. But the good jam is out, and the good jam does not come out for nothing.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Fern came in beaming about some flower of a word you built. She doesn't beam. Whatever you did in that Conservatory, do it again.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: She stood in my kitchen a full minute deciding how to say it, then said 'good hands' and left. From Fern that's a sonnet.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I pressed an extra flower into the day's post for luck. Don't ask which letter. Luck spoils if you look straight at it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You left a room unfinished. Good. A room will keep till tomorrow; a person won't always. He never learned that one.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: He'd sit up all hours rather than leave a puzzle half-done. I'd find the candle drowned and him asleep on the blotter. Don't be him. Be you, with breakfast.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The room will brag about being difficult, mind. Let it. Rooms need their little victories same as the rest of us.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There's cat hair on your sleeve and I have never seen you happier. Dewey has that effect. One step's a bargain.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: He'll pretend it never happened, of course. Cats keep their books in a currency of dignity. But he slept outside your door an hour. I saw.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There's a lint brush on the hall table now. Permanent fixture. Consider it his gift to you, by way of me.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Someone in this house is pressing flowers in a book today because of you. I'll say no more. Housekeepers see everything.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Kindness travels oddly in a place like this — down the dumbwaiter, up the chimneys. It always arrives, though. Always.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You keep on like this and I'll have to start a second ledger just for the household's moods improving. Paperwork I'd welcome, for once.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Spent to the last step again. You and the master both — hand you a lovely evening and you'll walk it to the bone. Sit. Toast. Then go be incorrigible.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I've buttered both sides. Don't tell the pantry ledger.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And take the short corridor today if it offers. It only offers to people it likes — that's not superstition, that's architecture.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: In at dusk with empty pockets and full eyes. That's not a scolding, pet — that's exactly how a good day looks from the doorway.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: He used to say the house measures its guests by what they're willing to spend on it. You'd have gotten on, the two of you. Terribly.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Go on, then. The house is already rearranging itself to show you something. I can hear it showing off from here.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Turned in early with steps still in the tin? Extravagant. The manor doesn't know what to do with restraint — it sulked in the corridors all night.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I told it: some guests have sense. It rattled a shutter at me. We've agreed to differ, the house and I, on the subject of you.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Either way, you're the best-rested soul under this roof, and I include the furniture. Use it on something lovely.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Library got the better of you before the light went, I hear. Shelves hold grudges, dear, but they never keep them — it'll sort kinder today.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And if it doesn't, tell Ellery I said she may glare at it. Her glare alphabetizes things.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Take the long way past the kitchen first. Fortified sorters make fewer misfiles — that's not folklore, that's breakfast.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Conservatory wouldn't bloom for you yesterday? Fern says some flowers only open for a rested gardener. Eat first. Then go make it flower.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: She sent up honey for your toast, by the way. Said the room owes you. Rooms pay their debts here, one way or another.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And talk to the flowers while you work. They don't understand a word, which is precisely what makes them such good company for a word-tired head.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: That Gallery ran you out of daylight, didn't it. Those paths tangle when you're tired, dear — they comb out easy on a full stomach.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I dust in there with my eyes half-shut, else the frames start suggesting routes. Ignore their advice. Take mine: porridge.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Start from a corner today. Corners are honest. It's the middles of things that lie to tired eyes.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Study kept its word from you yesterday. It kept his words from everyone for thirty years, so don't take it personally. Take toast.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: That room loved him best, I think. It'll come round to you the way he would have — slowly, then all at once, then forever.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Read his definitions out loud in there, if you're stuck. The room wrote them to be spoken. Most true things were.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Vestibule scrambled you out of the light, did it? Cheeky little room. It once turned 'welcome mat' into something unrepeatable and wouldn't turn it back for a week.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Letters unscramble kinder after breakfast, pet. It's practically science.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Try saying the jumble aloud on your way past. Half those scrambles are just words standing on their heads for attention.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Stuck on the Staircase till dusk, one rung shy? Word ladders are like real ones, dear — never look at the top, only the next step.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The master fell off that staircase for three days once. CORD to WARM, I think it was. He came down for meals and dignity, in that order.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Leave your pride on the landing and take the rungs one letter at a time. The Staircase respects a steady climber more than a clever one.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Darkroom kept its secrets past sunset, then. Ciphers are just words being shy, pet — and shy things come out for the patient and the fed.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Start with the little words today. Even in code, an 'A' alone is usually an 'A' being dramatic about it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And leave the door cracked for the light. Secrets keep better in the dark, but they're solved better out of it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Linen Closet crossed you up before the light went? It folds its clues like fitted sheets — nobody gets those right the first evening.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Try the downs first today. The acrosses in that closet are terrible show-offs; the downs just want to be useful.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And if a clue seems to be about towels, it is never about towels. That closet thinks itself very deep.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Music Room sang you out of steps, I hear. Rhymes dry up when you chase them, dear — they're cats that way. Look busy with your tea and one will land in your lap.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The piano in there still won't rhyme anything with 'orange.' It's been sulking about it since before my time.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Hum on your way up, pet. A primed ear rhymes twice as fast — choir trick. Housekeepers know a few.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: My Pantry outran you last night, did it? Don't be embarrassed — that room counts faster than a greengrocer at closing. It's the only impatient room I keep.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Between us: it softens for anyone who's eaten. Racing a larder on an empty stomach is asking the joke to write itself, pet.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Go in with a category in your teeth — fruits, say, or things that rhyme with 'jam.' A running start beats a clever one in there.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You said it. You actually said it out loud. I dusted that landing for years and never once — oh, sit down, dear, I'm going to cry into the marmalade.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The whole house came down two inches overnight. Settled, like a held breath let go. I heard every beam do it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There's cake for breakfast. Don't argue. Some mornings outrank the meal plan.

nodes.summary: Mrs. Bramble cried into the marmalade. Happily.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You've the same crease he had, right here, when a word wouldn't come. The master. I did his rooms thirty years. You may ask me one thing about him today, and I may even answer.

nodes.summary: Mrs. Bramble kept the master's rooms for thirty years.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Kind. Impossible. He'd stand in the Library till midnight arguing with a dictionary like it owed him money. Then one day the arguing stopped, and I still can't tell you which silence was worse.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: There. That's your one thing. The kettle's boiling and I've dusted my eyes quite enough for a Tuesday.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: He struck that word from every book in the house, you know. Ink over ink over ink. I thought it was scholarship. It wasn't. It was grief with a good vocabulary.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I brought his supper up the night he finished the last book. He said 'there — now it can't hurt anyone.' As if a word were a wasp. As if the hurt weren't already in the house.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: That's why I'm glad of you, pet. Somebody has to un-strike it. The house has been waiting for hands that would.

nodes.summary: The erasure wasn't scholarship. It was grief.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Here. The pantry key. It was his rule that guests earn it, and his rule that I decide when. Warm hands, warm bread, warm house — that's the whole economy of the place.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mind the third shelf. The preserves up there predate me, and I've chosen to respect their seniority.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And if the Pantry challenges you to one of its counting games while you're in there — that's its way of saying hello. Rude little room. My favorite.

nodes.summary: Earned the pantry key. Bramble's highest honor.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: A bookmark? For me? Oh — it's been a long time since anyone gave me something that wasn't a chore list.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Take this: his old tea tin. It rattles. He never let me look inside; I never let me look inside either. Yours now.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And if you do look — don't tell me what's in it. After thirty years, the rattle and I have an understanding.

nodes.summary: Gave Mrs. Bramble a bookmark; received the master's rattling tea tin.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Another bookmark? You'll have me reading above my station. It goes in the recipe book — page with the lemon cake, so I find it often.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Go on with you now, before I start saving you the good crusts on purpose. ...I already do. Well. Now it's official.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And no, before you ask — lemon cake is not a bribe if it is scheduled. Thursday. Be hungry.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Rain again on the east windows — which is odd, dear, because the east windows face indoors now. I've stopped filing complaints.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The house does its own weather the way some men do their own taxes: confidently, and wrong.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Still — indoor rain keeps the ferns glad and the dust humble. A house could do worse for hobbies.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If a door won't open, it's not locked, it's shy. Knock twice and mean it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The cellar door wants three knocks and a compliment, but the cellar has always been needy.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And never rattle a handle. You wouldn't like being rattled, and doors have longer memories than either of us.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Thirty-one rooms yesterday, thirty-three today. I don't dust the new ones till they've decided to stay.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Learned that the hard way. Polished a parlor top to bottom in '09 and it was a linen cupboard by supper. Beautiful cupboard, mind.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You can tell a room's decided to stay when it starts collecting dust with a bit of pride. Like a dog settling into its basket.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If Dewey sits on a paper, that paper matters. If he sits on you, you matter. The cat is never wrong; it's infuriating.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: He sat on the master's last good pen for a week once. We only understood why after. I don't ask the cat questions anymore; I just thank him on a delay.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The kettle knows the day's weather before the sky does. Rolling boil this morning. Take that as you will.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: A rolling boil means a finding sort of day, historically. I keep records. Well — I keep feelings, in the shape of records.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: So: a finding day. Wear the coat with the deep pockets.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You're gathering his scraps, I see. When they start to rhyme in your head — that's when you take the stairs to the top. Not before, and not alone: I'll have tea waiting either way.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: And don't fear the door. It's not a test you can fail, whatever the Portrait implies. It's a door that misses being knocked on.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Whatever happens up there, there's tea after. That's not comfort, dear, that's policy.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Portrait on the landing — don't mind his scowl. He scowled at everyone, alive. It was practically affection.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I dust his frame Thursdays and tell him the news. He pretends the paint can't hear. We're both terrible liars, and it's the nicest hour of my week.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If you find the Linen Closet today, mind it doesn't rope you into its little crossword. Or do let it — but count your steps. That closet flirts in clues.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: It asked me for a seven-letter word for 'housekeeper' once. I said 'BRAMBLE' and it's been sweet on me since.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Hear the Pantry rattling its shelves? It wants someone to play its naming game. Greedy thing — it'd have you list cheeses till Michaelmas if the steps held out.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Humor it now and then, pet. A pantry that feels appreciated keeps the biscuits from going wherever biscuits go in this house.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Music Room was humming to itself before dawn. Rhyming weather. If it asks you for a word to finish a verse, give it a good one — it remembers a lazy rhyme for years.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: It once held a grudge over 'moon' and 'June' for an entire winter. Standards, that room.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Staircase is in one of its ladder moods — changing one letter of itself per landing. Went up as STAIRS yesterday, came down as STORES. The luggage was confused.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Take it slow if you climb it today. One rung, one letter, no vaulting. Same advice I gave the master; same advice he ignored.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If a room goes red-lit and whispery on you, that's the Darkroom. Everything it says is in code, even the pleasantries. Nod politely and bring a pencil.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: It ciphered my shopping list once. Took me two days to learn I'd bought twelve XQFFS. They were eggs. Lovely eggs, in fairness.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: The Vestibule's rearranged its welcome sign again. This morning it says 'CLEMEOW.' Either it means WELCOME or the cat has learned to spell. Both alarm me.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If it jumbles a word at you on your way through, jumble one back. It respects the effort and unhands your coat quicker.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Small room, big heart, terrible spelling. We keep it for the company.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: We'll talk properly tomorrow, dear — these floors won't scold themselves.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Unless the ceiling comes down. Then knock twice and bring a bucket, there's a dear.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Off with you now. Daylight's a budget, and you've spent enough of it on an old housekeeper.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mind the runner in the hall — it moved overnight and I refuse to chase it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Third time this month. I suspect the hall of encouraging it.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Kettle's always on. That's not a metaphor, it's a fire hazard I've made peace with.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Cup's poured if you want it walking past. No obligation. There's always no obligation, and there's always a cup.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: You've crumbs — no, other cheek. There. Presentable.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Can't have the rooms thinking I feed you carelessly. I have a reputation with the wallpaper.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If you see the good silver in an odd room, leave it. It's sulking.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: It gets like this every spring. By June it will be back in the sideboard, acting as though nothing happened.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Sheets on the line in the courtyard that isn't there on Wednesdays. Timing, dear, is everything in this house.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: If you meet the courtyard before I do, tell it the sheets are winning.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: It's a better house with you in it, pet. Even the drafts think so.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Now shoo, before I say something soppier and the wallpaper starts talking.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mrs. Bramble hums something old and out of tune, polishing a doorknob that was already bright.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: She catches you looking, winks, and goes on humming. The doorknob has never been brighter.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Before you go rattling doorknobs, pet — sit a moment. There's a thing I've dusted around for years and never once said out loud.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Six candles at his desk, always six. Near the end he let one gutter out each night — and I never dared relight them. Some housekeeping isn't yours to do.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Put it in your journal, love. It's evidence, even if saying it still feels like tidying his grave.

nodes.summary: Mrs. Bramble's testimony: six candles, let out one by one.
